newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude steady, March MidEast crude traded.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude steady, March MidEast crude traded.

text.p: Asian crude prices were mostly steady on Tuesday in quiet dealings but with lingering MidEast crude for March liftings trading.

Traders said two majors exchanged a cargo of Umm Shaif at a premium of 10 to 20 cents over ADNOC. Some traders said the price was nearer +10 cents than +20 cents, down from earlier deals around +30 cents.

Players said a Dubai March cargo was hanging over the market from a major, which players had thought had been awarded in the India March buying tender over the weekend. The major was seen offering the March/April spread on Dubai swaps.
Traders said the cargo was the last remaining for March trading.
Oman MPM released its January official selling price at $22.50, surprising traders because it indicated a differential to Dubai of $1.14, up from $1.04 last month.

Traders said they had expected a slight narrowing of the differential, especially as the market was in the midst of refinery run cuts because of poor margins and was next considering April trading, when there is a seasonal fall in demand anyhow. "Forward projections for margins are still bad," said on trader.
The regional market was still assessing the March trading month, but some players were eager to sell Minas and Bach Ho crudes amid a general expectation of a weaker market.
Some Minas has been on offer at premiums of 50 to 65 cents, well below February levels of more than $1.00.
Traders said a major sold a cargo of Cossack crude at Tapis quotes plus 15 cents, five cent below levels offered by a producer.
